observations: Single photo shows a bare engine assembly (no vehicle body), sitting on a floor/pallet with wiring harness and fuel lines visible.
Appears to be a diesel engine based on visible glow-plug wiring and what looks like an injection pump, but no manufacturer badge, engine code, or model plate is legible.
No odometer, no video, no close-up of any ID plate or engine code stamp is shown.
Watermark reads 'CAMON 40' with camera EXIF-style text, unrelated to the engine's identity.
Surface has grime and corrosion consistent with a used, outdoor/salvage-stored part, but nothing confirms mileage or internal condition.

claims.evidence: Seller's own text immediately says 'direct from Belgium' — the two origin claims conflict with each other.
Conflicts with the preceding 'Direct Japan' claim in the same listing text.
No written warranty document or shop stamp shown in photo.
Photo shows a used-looking engine but no import/customs paperwork or shipping tag visible.
No start-up video, compression test, or meter reading shown.
An audio claim; nothing in a still photo can confirm sound.
No odometer or mileage sticker visible; this is a stand-alone engine, not the full vehicle.
No close-up of valve cover bolts, seals, or factory paint marks to confirm it hasn't been disassembled.

risks.risk: Engine make and model cannot be confirmed, which drives most of the price.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine code plate/stamp (usually on block near gearbox mount) or any manufacturer badge.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced at all without this — price range for 'unknown diesel engine' is too wide to set a worst case.

risks.risk: Actual running condition (compression, oil leaks, smoke) unverified.
risks.proof: Video of engine running/idling with sound, plus smoke check.

risks.risk: Internal wear or prior major repair (e.g., rebuilt block) not visible from outside.
risks.proof: Photos of valve cover removed, or service/repair history documents.

risks.risk: Origin/import story inconsistent, raising doubt about documentation and true source.
risks.proof: Photo of shipping/import documents or customs paperwork matching one consistent origin.
risks.if_unproven: Treated as unverified origin, no premium for 'direct import' claimed.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/model stamp or manufacturer plate.
Video of the engine running, with audible idle sound.
Photo of any import/customs documentation showing country of origin.
Photo of valve cover area and bolts to assess if engine has been opened.
response.reason: The engine's make and model cannot be read from the single photo, and this is the key driver of price for an engine; the seller's origin claims are also internally contradictory, so a model/code photo and consistent documentation are needed before even a worst-case price can be set.
